sense: a plan of how something will be made

evidence: Cic. Q. fr. 2.5.3: quam quantum ex fōrmā jūdicābāmus
Cic. Fam. 2.8.1: cum fōrmam reī pūblicae vīderim, quāle aedificium futūrum sit scīre possim
terms.comment: The outline from which a building is judged before it stands (Lewis & Short: “an outline, plan, design (of an architect)”). To draw a design is dēscrībere (M-O s.v. design, citing Egger), as Archimedes drew his figures in the dust (fōrmīs, quās in pulvere dēscrīpserat, Liv. 25.31.9, Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: a drawing, a plan; the layout of a building
terms.comment: Cicero’s word for the plan of a house, which is to be fitted to its use (Off. 1.138).

evidence: M-O s.v. floor plan, ground plan, blueprint
terms.comment: Vitruvius’s Greek term (ἰχνογραφία), for the technical drawing.

phrases.latin: domus erit ēgregia; magis enim cernī jam poterat quam quantum ex fōrmā jūdicābāmus
phrases.english: the house will be splendid: one can see more of it now than we could judge from the plan

forma.html: De Vaan 233–234, s.v. fōrma, prints the o long; Ernout–Meillet “stress the length of o”, which he takes for a recent lengthening of short o before r and a consonant (Leumann 1977: 114).

sources: Lewis & Short: forma · Lewis & Short: descriptio · Lewis & Short: ichnographia
Michiel de Vaan, Etymological Dictionary of Latin and the other Italic Languages (2008), pp. 233–234.
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. design (vb.); floor plan, ground plan, blueprint.
